deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, no derivations, no computations. It is a heavily corrected draft of the methodological introduction to Riemann's posthumous fragment on the mechanics of the ear. That fragment was edited by Henle and printed in 1867 as 'Mechanik des Ohres' (Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin) and is reprinted in the Gesammelte Werke. The page is marked 'p. 6' and continues the previous page's programme of comparing a theory of the organ with experience.

Content, in order:

(1) Following this method, one must first establish the 'Leistungen' (performances) of the hearing organ. That is: with what sharpness, fineness and fidelity the ear perceives sound waves with respect to pitch (Tonhöhe), timbre (Klangfarbe), loudness (Stärke) and direction (Richtung). This must be fixed by observation and experiment as precisely as possible.

(2) Riemann first wrote that he assumes these facts as known and refers to Helmholtz's 'Die Lehre von den Tonempfindungen als physiologische Grundlage für die Theorie der Musik' (1863). He then struck this and recast it. One finds there collected the recent advances in our knowledge of the perception of tones, made chiefly by Helmholtz himself. Helmholtz's book and its historical notes sufficiently guarantee the facts.

(3) A courtesy passage. Since Riemann must oppose some of the conclusions Helmholtz drew from the experiments, he cannot pass over in silence how much he values Helmholtz's great merits on this subject.

(4) A struck-through and rewritten sentence, partly illegible. It appears to say that observation of the phenomena, not theory, is the necessary foundation for a theory of the ear's motions.

(5) The anatomy of the ear is likewise assumed known. The reader is asked to consult an illustrated anatomical handbook if needed. The newest results on the structure of the cochlea and of the ear in general are presented in the just-published third Lieferung of volume 2 of Henle's Handbuch der (systematischen) Anatomie des Menschen. This dates the draft to c. 1866.

(6) The parts relevant to the problem are named: the sound-conducting apparatus (the ossicles) and the labyrinth, which consists of the vestibule, the semicircular canals and the cochlea.

(7) Statement of method. First infer from the required performances what the structure of these parts must achieve. Then, from the structure of the individual parts and from the task they must fulfil, determine the more precise conditions required for a satisfactory solution of the task. The sentence continues on the next page ('zu einer genügenden Lösung der Aufgabe erforderlich ist').

The next page begins the analysis of the tympanic apparatus. That apparatus transmits air pressure to the labyrinth water, and the ossicles move as one rigid body rotating about an axis.

No implicit mathematical steps exist on this page to fill in.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.

Historically the page is consistent with the known context: Helmholtz's Tonempfindungen appeared in 1863, and Henle's volume 2, third Lieferung (covering the sense organs) appeared in 1866, the year of Riemann's death.

results.what: Methodological programme: deduce the mechanical requirements of the ear's sound-conducting apparatus from its measured perceptual performance (pitch, timbre, loudness, direction), then derive the detailed conditions from the anatomy. This is accompanied by a critical but respectful stance toward Helmholtz's theory of the ossicles.
results.modern_name: Inverse or functional approach to auditory biomechanics; middle-ear transfer-function analysis
results.usually_credited_to: Helmholtz (1863 Tonempfindungen; 1868 'Die Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen und des Trommelfells'); Riemann's own fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' (published 1867 by Henle)

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely prose: a draft of the introduction to Riemann's known, published fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres', with its references to Helmholtz and Henle. It contains no mathematics and no result beyond what the published version contains.
transcription_corrections: The interlinear 'die Schallh.[?]' is almost certainly 'die Tonhöhe'. The intended list is: Tonhöhe, Klangfarbe, Stärke und Richtung.
'wie möglich[?] / als möglich[?] festgestellt' should read: 'so genau als möglich festgestellt werden'.
The marginal '{+Cutis[?]+}' near 'zu seiner Theorie der Bewegungen' is probably not 'Cutis'; it may be a word such as 'Citat' or an insertion mark. The reading is uncertain.
'Auf diesem Gange' may be 'Auf diesem Wege' (compare the published text: 'Auf diesem Wege müssten zunächst die Leistungen des Gehörorgans festgestellt werden'). The word is uncertain in the image.
The title on the page is Helmholtz's book: 'Die Lehre von den Tonempfindungen als physiologische Grundlage für die Theorie der Musik'. The first 'physiologische' is struck and rewritten.

In 'Der schallleitende Apparat, der für unseren Zweck in Betracht kommen, sind' the clause was meant as 'Die Bestandtheile, die für unseren Zweck in Betracht kommen, sind der schallleitende Apparat, die Gehörknöchelchen und das Labyrinth'. The draft is grammatically unfinished.
'Vorhofe' (vestibule) is correct. The labyrinth is listed as Vorhof, Bogengänge, Schnecke.
